title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the neighbouring pages: X is a smooth 'multiplicité' (a manifold, orbifold or stack; in the application a compactified moduli space of curves), and D is a divisor with normal crossings in X. At a point x, let I(x) be the set of local branches of D through x. The intersections of subsets of these branches give germs of submanifolds; they form the poset Fl(I(x))^0, the subsets of I(x) with reversed order, graded by codimension = cardinality.

On the previous page Grothendieck defined:
- D_d, whose points are pairs (x, V) with V a codimension-d germ cut out by d branches. This is the normalization of the codimension-d stratum. The map D_d → X is an immersion locale of codimension d.
- D̃_d, whose points are triples (x, V, W) with V ⊂ W and W a branch (codimension 1). The map D̃_d → D_d is étale of degree d, and there is a map D̃_d → D_1.

He then generalized to D_J for a finite ordered set J carrying a codimension function. A point of D_J is a pair (x, φ), where φ: J ↪ Fl(I(x))^0 is a strictly codimension-compatible embedding (a 'system of coordinate functions').

On this page he states:
1. If J has an extremal element e_J of codimension d = d(J) (the hypothesis is written, then struck out), then D_J is smooth. The canonical map D_J → X is a local immersion of codimension d, and it factors through D_d. The 'exception' is J a single element of codimension 0, where D_J = X; since D_0 = X this is really consistent rather than an exception.
2. Examples:
   - J a single element of codimension d gives D_d.
   - J = {e_J (codimension d) > e' (codimension 1)} gives D̃_d.
3. Reconstruction of D_J from D_d and D̃_d. Let D'_d → D_d be the principal G_d-torsor attached to the degree-d étale cover D̃_d → D_d, with G_d ≅ S_d. It is the torsor of total orderings of the d branches through V, i.e. the 'frame bundle' of the cover. It is identified with D_{I(d)}, where I(d) is the chain 0 < 1 < … < d, a maximal flag of codimension d. Indeed, a codimension-compatible embedding of this chain into the subsets of the d branches is a full flag ∅ ⊂ {a1} ⊂ … ⊂ {a1,…,ad}, i.e. an ordering of the branches.
4. The next page then gives D_J ≅ D'_d ×^{S_d} H(J). Here H(J) is the finite S_d-set of codimension-compatible order-embeddings J → P([1,d])^op. He also gives functoriality D_J → D_{J'} for J' ↪ J.
5. The oblique marginal note says roughly that the description D'_d = D_{I(d)} holds only under an extra hypothesis involving the ordering, the group written Ḡ_d, and a 'feuilletage'. It is largely illegible.

Purpose: to build a combinatorial–geometric dictionary for the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}. Strata, together with incidence data, are indexed by posets with codimension functions and expressed as associated bundles of a single S_d-torsor per codimension. This is the local monodromy of the branches, which for M̄_{g,ν} is the automorphism data of the dual graphs.
errors: The extremal-element hypothesis (struck out in the first lines) is actually necessary. Take J = two incomparable elements of codimension 1. Then D_J is the space of ordered pairs of distinct branches, which is D'_2, of codimension 2 rather than d(J) = 1. For two incomparable codimension-2 elements, D_J is not even equidimensional: the union of the images can have 3 or 4 branches. So 'immersion locale de codim d(J)' and the formula D_J ≅ D'_d ×^{S_d} H(J) with d = d(J) need J to have a greatest element in codimension (equivalently, d(J) := codimension of the join). Alternatively, 'dim totale' must be defined as the size of the union, but that is not determined by J alone.
The 'sauf dans le cas d(J) = 0' clause is not a real exception, since D_0 = X (as stated on the previous page). It reads as an inessential hedge.
Minor: D_J → X is a local immersion, so it is 'smooth' only in the sense of D_J being a smooth multiplicity mapping non-injectively onto the stratum closure. This is fine, but worth noting.

ideas.what: Normalizations D_d of the codimension-d strata of a normal crossings divisor, with the degree-d étale cover D̃_d of 'branch through V' and the associated S_d-torsor of orderings of branches (D'_d = D_{I(d)}, the full flags)
ideas.modern_name: Normalized strata of an snc/nc divisor; the monodromy torsor of the branches; 'ordered' strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (Deligne's Hodge II used D^{(d)} and orientation local systems ε^d, 1971)
ideas.where_published: Related material in SGA 7 / Grothendieck–Murre on tame fundamental groups along normal crossings divisors; not this formalism

ideas.what: Indexing generalized strata D_J by finite posets with codimension function, via embeddings into the reversed subset lattice of local branches; contravariant functoriality D_J → D_{J'} in J
ideas.modern_name: Stratification functor / diagram of strata; exit-path or entrance-path category of the stratification; poset-indexed data of the boundary complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Thuillier (2007), Abramovich–Caporaso–Payne (2015) generalized cone complexes, and stratified-space exit-path categories (MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie)

ideas.what: Expression of every D_J as an associated bundle D'_d ×^{S_d} H(J), with H(J) a finite S_d-set of codimension-compatible poset embeddings into P([1,d])^op
ideas.modern_name: Strata as quotients of the ordered stratum by a symmetric group, i.e. the stacky/orbifold boundary complex with S_d-symmetry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Abramovich–Caporaso–Payne (generalized cone complexes as colimits of cones modulo finite groups); Harper and others for nc divisors

missed.claim: Grothendieck organizes all incidence strata of a normal crossings boundary as a functor from (posets with codimension function) to multiplicities. Every member of the functor is the associated bundle of one S_d-torsor per codimension with a combinatorial S_d-set H(J). This is essentially the data later packaged as the generalized cone complex / tropicalization of the boundary (ACP 2015 for M̄_{g,n}), here in a geometric, torsor-theoretic form aimed explicitly at the structure at infinity of M_{g,ν}.
missed.quote: on a un reconstruction D_J à partir de D_d et de D̃_d, via le torseur principal (torseur sous G_d) sur D_d associé : D̃_d, soit D'_d, qui s'identifie aussi à D_{I(d)}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A historical precursor to the boundary-complex / tropical-moduli formalism. Mathematically it is now standard, so its main value is historical.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but essentially standard bookkeeping of normal crossings strata and the S_d-monodromy of branches. The poset-indexed functorial packaging foreshadows boundary/cone complexes, but specialists would find nothing mathematically new.
transcription_corrections: Equation label is (153), not (15): '(153) D_J → X'. The previous page used (152) and the next page starts at (154).
'sauf dans le cas où d(J) =0 i.e. J se réduit à un seul élément' — the superscript '=0 i.e. J' is an insertion above the line.
'D_J = X' is written over a struck-out letter (likely 'D_0'), i.e. 'D_J = D_0 = X'.
Chain diagram labels read 'd, d−1, …, 2, 1, 0' (the '2' is partly overwritten).

Margin is likely 'Mais l'expression de D'_d comme D_{I(d)} ne vaut que si on a une [?] … des Ḡ_d … feuilletage … petit … d'élément … dans les … codim.' It is largely illegible; the group written there appears to be Ḡ_d (or 𝔊_d), matching 𝔊_d on the next page.
